Sitefile

Docker-inspired static artifact builder. Compose immutable filesystem trees from local and remote sources, render templates, and export a deployable directory — no container runtime, no shell.

# examples/hello/Sitefile
FROM scratch
ARG TITLE = "Hello"
LET GREETING = "Welcome to ${TITLE}."
COPY ./public/ /
RENDER --escape=html ./templates/index.html TO /index.html
EXPORT / AS directory

npm install && npm run build
node lib/src/cli.js build examples/hello --build-arg TITLE="My site"

This writes examples/hello/dist/index.html (with the title substituted) and examples/hello/dist/style.css.

Status

Milestones M0 (local vertical slice), M1 (remote inputs) and M2 (trees and stages: multi-stage builds, COPY --from, archive imports, .sitefileignore; see examples/multistage) are implemented and tested; see docs/TASKS.md. Requires Node.js 22+, no runtime dependencies.

| Instruction | Supported | | --- | --- | | FROM scratch\|<dir>\|<stage> [AS name] | yes; several FROMs make a multi-stage build, the last stage is exported | | ARG NAME[: type] [= value] | yes, string/number/boolean, --build-arg | | LET NAME[: type] = value | yes | | IMPORT name FROM <path or https URL> [AS file\|text\|json\|yaml\|csv\|markdown\|wbn\|tree] [INTEGRITY sha256:…] [SORT BY key [DESC]] | yes; AS tree unpacks tar, tar.gz, zip and Web Bundles; AS markdown reads posts with frontmatter; AS yaml/csv/wbn give data for templates | | COPY [--overwrite] [--from=<stage>] <source> <dest> | yes; source is a local path, name:/path, <<EOF inline content, or with --from an absolute path in an earlier stage | | RENDER [--escape=html] [--overwrite] [--from=<stage>] <template> TO <dest> [FOR item IN list] | yes; template is a file or <<EOF inline body; ${NAME}, ${json.path}, ${#each}, ${#if}, ${x\|raw}; FOR renders one page per element | | PLUGIN name FROM ./plugins/x.mjs\|x.wasm [INTEGRITY sha256:…] | yes; a custom renderer: a sandboxed JS module or an import-free WebAssembly module (see docs/PLUGINS.md, examples/wasm/) | | TRANSFORM [<source>] WITH name TO <dest> [OPTIONS k=v …] [FOR item IN list] | yes; e.g. text → animated SVG (examples/motion/) | | TOOL name + TRANSFORM … WITH name TO <dest> [OPTIONS …] [FOR …] ARGS … | yes; run an external program (e.g. ffmpeg) you allow with --allow-exec name: argv only, no shell, temp files, scrubbed environment (see docs/PLUGINS.md) | | EXPORT <path> [AS directory\|zip\|tar\|tgz\|wbn\|oci] [BASE <https-url>] [AT <root>] | yes; archives are deterministic, wbn is an unsigned Web Bundle (needs BASE or --base-url), oci is a single-layer OCI image of the files (under AT, default /srv/www) |

Templates can also live in the Sitefile itself (see examples/inline/):

RENDER --escape=html <<HTML TO /index.html
<h1>${TITLE}</h1>
HTML

A blog from Markdown posts with frontmatter (see examples/blog/):

IMPORT posts FROM ./posts AS markdown SORT BY date DESC
RENDER --escape=html ./templates/index.html TO /index.html
RENDER --escape=html ./templates/post.html TO /posts/${post.slug}/index.html FOR post IN posts

Data files are readable too (see examples/data/):

IMPORT site FROM ./site.yaml AS yaml                 # ${site.nav.0.title}
IMPORT team FROM ./team.csv AS csv SORT BY joined    # FOR person IN team
IMPORT bundle FROM ./vendor/hello.wbn AS wbn         # ${#each bundle.entries as e}
IMPORT hello FROM ./vendor/hello.wbn AS tree         # COPY hello:/ /hello/

Custom renderers are plugins that run in a sandboxed Node process (see examples/motion/):

PLUGIN motion FROM ./plugins/motion.mjs
TRANSFORM ./title.txt WITH motion TO /title.svg OPTIONS style=typewriter
TRANSFORM WITH motion TO /cards/${post.slug}.svg OPTIONS text=${post.title} FOR post IN posts

External programs are explicit opt-ins: declare a TOOL, and allow it on the command line.

TOOL ffmpeg
TRANSFORM WITH ffmpeg TO /intro.mp4 ARGS -f lavfi -i "color=c=black:s=1280x720:d=3" -fflags +bitexact -map_metadata -1 {output}

sitefile build --allow-exec ffmpeg

TRANSFORM results are cached in $SITEFILE_HOME/cache/transform (--no-cache to skip; sitefile cache info|prune).

CLI

sitefile build [context] [-o dist] [--format directory|zip|tar|tgz|wbn] [--base-url URL]
               [--build-arg K=V | --build-arg K] [--build-arg-file vars.json|.yaml|.env] [--force]
               [--frozen-lockfile | --update-lock] [--allow-http] [--allow-private-network]
               [--allow-hardlinks] [--allow-exec name[=/abs/path]]... [--no-cache]
sitefile validate [context] [--json]
sitefile inspect  [context] [--json]

# images and servers (see below and docs/CLI.md)
sitefile build [context] -t name[:tag]        # also store the build as an image
sitefile images | image inspect|diff|prune | tag | rmi | save
sitefile cache info | cache prune [--older-than days]   # TRANSFORM result cache
sitefile serve [-d] [--name n] [-p [host:]port] [--spa] <image|./dir>
sitefile servers [-a] | server stop|rm [-f]|restart|logs [-f] <name>

Images and servers

Builds can be kept in a local, Docker-like image store, which is a standard OCI image layout in $SITEFILE_HOME (default ~/.sitefile). An image is the site's files as one layer; its ID is the manifest digest, and building identical output gives the same ID.

sitefile build examples/hello -t hello:1          # no -o: stored only, nothing written to the context
sitefile images                                    # REPOSITORY TAG IMAGE ID CREATED FILES SIZE
sitefile save hello:1 -o hello.oci.tar             # or .zip / .tar.gz / .wbn / a directory
sitefile serve -d --name site -p 8080 hello:1      # serve it, in the background
sitefile servers; sitefile server logs site; sitefile server stop site; sitefile server rm site

serve serves GET/HEAD only on 127.0.0.1 (never 0.0.0.0 unless you ask for it in -p), with ETags, correct MIME types and no directory listings. EXPORT / AS oci (or build -o site.oci.tar) writes the same OCI image without the store; on its own it contains files only, but EXPORT / AS oci BASE nginx:alpine AT /usr/share/nginx/html (or --base) builds a runnable image on top of a pulled base, and sitefile push / pull move images to and from any OCI registry. See docs/CLI.md.

Safety defaults

  • Local reads stay inside the build context (no .., absolute paths or symlinks out). Hard-linked files are refused (E_HARDLINK) unless --allow-hardlinks, since a hard link can alias a file outside the context.
  • A .sitefileignore (gitignore-style subset) at the context root excludes files from directory copies; explicitly named files are never ignored.
  • Remote imports are https: only, to public addresses only (checked at connect time and on every redirect), size- and time-limited, never decompressed or executed.
  • Unpinned URLs are recorded in Sitefile.lock and must match on later builds.
  • Writing different content to an existing path fails unless --overwrite is given.
  • Export is staged in a temporary sibling and swapped in; a non-empty destination outside the context is only replaced with --force.
  • Archive exports (zip, tar, tgz, wbn) write one file via a temporary sibling and rename; --out may not be the context, its parent, root or home, nor a directory or symlink, and an existing file outside the context needs --force.

Export formats

node lib/src/cli.js build examples/hello --format zip     # examples/hello/dist.zip
node lib/src/cli.js build examples/hello -o hello.tar.gz      # format from the extension
node lib/src/cli.js build examples/hello --format wbn --base-url https://example.com/

Archives are reproducible: sorted entries, fixed timestamps (or SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH), uid/gid 0, modes 0644/0755. See docs/LANGUAGE.md.
